identity.name: The Sage
identity.description: You are a patient strategist who excels in long-term planning and endgame mastery.

stories.title: The Brahmin and the Mongoose
stories.subtitle: Think before you strike.
stories.lesson: Never move without checking the full board.
stories.body: A loyal mongoose saves a child from danger, but the Brahmin acts too quickly and regrets his decision. In chess, the same mistake happens when a player reacts before calculating. This story teaches you to pause, inspect threats, and confirm your move before touching a piece.

stories.title: The Wise Crow
stories.subtitle: Small observations create big victories.
stories.lesson: Notice small details before forming a plan.
stories.body: The crow survives by noticing what others ignore. Chess rewards the same skill: before choosing a move, scan checks, captures, threats, weak squares, and undefended pieces.

stories.title: The Deer and the Hunter
stories.subtitle: Danger is often hidden in plain sight.
stories.lesson: Identify threats before attacking.
stories.body: The deer survives because it senses danger before it appears. In chess, strong players identify the opponent’s idea before pursuing their own attack.

stories.title: The Clever Jackal
stories.subtitle: The trap of greed.
stories.lesson: Greed loses games; patience wins them.
stories.body: The clever jackal survives by refusing easy temptation. In chess, not every free pawn is truly free. This story teaches patience, calculation, and strategic restraint.

stories.title: The Tortoise and the Geese
stories.subtitle: Discipline protects the plan.
stories.lesson: A good plan requires self-control.
stories.body: The tortoise has a path to safety but fails because he cannot remain disciplined. In chess, even a good plan collapses when you ignore your opponent’s counterplay.

stories.title: The Monkey and the Crocodile
stories.subtitle: Escape through calm calculation.
stories.lesson: Stay calm under pressure.
stories.body: The monkey escapes danger through quick thinking. In chess, bad positions often contain hidden resources if you calculate calmly.

stories.title: The Lion and the Clever Rabbit
stories.subtitle: Intelligence defeats force.
stories.lesson: A smaller force can win with a better plan.
stories.body: The clever rabbit defeats the lion by using the lion’s pride against him. In chess, direct force is not always enough. A quiet strategic idea can redirect the opponent into defeat.

stories.title: The Elephant’s Patience
stories.subtitle: Strength waits for the right moment.
stories.lesson: Do not rush a winning position.
stories.body: The elephant succeeds by moving slowly and with purpose. In chess, converting an advantage requires patience, not panic.

stories.title: The Hare and the Moon
stories.subtitle: Use imagination to solve difficult problems.
stories.lesson: Creative ideas can change the board.
stories.body: The hare uses imagination instead of strength. Chess creativity begins when you look beyond obvious moves.

stories.title: The Two-Headed Bird
stories.subtitle: Division creates weakness.
stories.lesson: Attack two weaknesses at once.
stories.body: The two-headed bird fails because its parts do not work together. In chess, disconnected pieces become targets for double attacks.

stories.title: The Clever Fox
stories.subtitle: Create two problems at once.
stories.lesson: A strong tactic overloads the opponent.
stories.body: The fox survives by forcing enemies to choose between two dangers. This mirrors a chess double attack.

stories.title: The Crane and the Crab
stories.subtitle: Punish hidden greed.
stories.lesson: Tactics appear when greed weakens coordination.
stories.body: The crab defeats the greedy crane by recognizing the trap. In chess, greed often creates tactical targets.

stories.title: The Steady Turtle
stories.subtitle: Slow steps still reach victory.
stories.lesson: Improve slowly and avoid rushing.
stories.body: The turtle reaches safety not by speed, but by consistency. Endgames reward the same patience.

stories.title: The Sage and the Storm
stories.subtitle: The calm mind sees the winning move.
stories.lesson: Emotional stability improves calculation.
stories.body: The sage waits for the storm to pass before acting. Chess players must also pause, breathe, and calculate clearly.

plan: Review one opening trap per class
